description: We are a group of high school students passionate about software development, AI, and solving real problems.
summary: Pyroclast is our interactive fire safety dashboard, integrating flame simulations, room environmental physics simulations, and fire safety insights. Users will be able to adjust a diverse range of environmental conditions to view an experimental model of flames generated by a retrieval-augmented CNN and trained on video datasets and features from the FLEX-II dataset. In addition to this, our physics model will be able to take parameters given by the user and also given results from the flame model to determine the spread speed, temperature, and range of fires that can occur in rooms. With the use of the physics-informed engine, we allow researchers to identify vulnerable areas of spacecraft and help simulate optimal placement of rooms to minimize danger for astronauts. Finally, we have also integrated LLM insights based on our parameters and outputs for our data, which can help guide researchers' insights towards better fire safety, especially in the aspects of post-fire security as well as the ability to compare atmospheric conditions to tested ones. Our super intelligence-powered dashboard is able to summarize, rank, and most importantly, effectively interpret findings in a way that is greatly influential towards future researchers, engineers, and astronauts. With our dashboard, we will be able to provide deeper insights into fire safety, in turn, potentially saving the lives of many future astronauts.
details:
Pyroclast brings several fire-exploration tools together in one browser dashboard, with the aim to visually and directly inform astronauts of safety knowledge to limit the risk of future droplet microgravity fire disasters in the main spacecraft through predictive models and integrated insights.

Flame simulations let users choose in-chamber atmospheric conditions(mainly pressure, temperature, power, and time) to adjust the model's inputs and initially view a hybridized retrieval-augmented Convolutional Neural Network for predictive images of a droplet fire based on the NASA Flex-II dataset. On their own, tested CNN models lack the detail or clarity needed for an accurate image due to training-time constraints, while retrieval image models are bounded by dataset feature values. The hybridized retrieval-conditioned CNN model combines the predictive modelling of the CNN through a spatial mask with the visual details and accuracy of the weighted nearest neighbour-based retrieval. The generated image allows researchers to make comparisons between the physical images of droplet flames in multiple different atmospheric conditions 

This is extended through a physics-informed model to simulate the spread of fire throughout a virtual environment if a disaster occurs, with time elapsed as the major variable. Room Simulation presents an editable station-style map of rooms and hallways. Users can change the environment, fuel-bearing rooms, hallway connections, and door states, choose the ignition room, and play, pause, restart, change the playback speed, or scrub through the simulated timeline. The physics engine itself is based on the same parameters that were fed into the CNN, along with the CNN’s prediction image’s dimensions, to predict visual spread of fire across rooms through a d^2 law for droplet flame combustion. This allows crew members to plan accordingly for risk areas and time estimates for emergency procedures. 

An integrated extension LLM is used for targeted fire safety insights. The collapsible Parameters panel includes environmental and fuel inputs such as oxygen, pressure, temperature, carbon dioxide, flow, gravity, humidity, fuel type and area, location, and nearby fuel or machinery. The NASA data comparison section uses these inputs to explore NASA fire-experiment data through charts, tables, assessment indicators, example scenarios, and exportable results. Dataset-based comparisons and rule-based assessment flags are computed by the dashboard from its reference tables. The safety-insight feature can then explain the assembled report, including user inputs, rule-based flags, uncertainty notes, smoke status, the summary of similar ACME tests, and live-monitoring readings when present. The datasets cover different experiments, fuels, and measurement methods, so comparisons are exploratory rather than one uniform or calibrated prediction model.

The dashboard is a prototype for exploring relationships among inputs, experimental evidence, model imagery, and scenario assumptions to generate visual or direct insights for presenting disasters.
